3: ## What This Is
4: 
5: Treads is a global nature-walk companion web application for casual walkers, curious parents, and amateur naturalists. On an outdoor walk, walkers photograph living organisms, an open-weight AI model identifies them, the server verifies and grounds facts exclusively in Wikipedia text, and audio voice notes can be recorded in any language. The entire journal, trail map, and life list live privately on the device in IndexedDB.

17: - [x] **CONS-04**: Permissions (camera, mic, location) are requested just-in-time at point of use with non-blocking inline fallback messaging if denied.
18: 
19: ### Walk Lifecycle & Tracking
20: 
21: - [ ] **WALK-01**: User can start a new walk session from `/walk` with a single tap, generating a unique session in IndexedDB.
22: - [ ] **WALK-02**: Active walk automatically resumes if the browser tab is reloaded, backgrounded, or restored after camera use (`endedAt == null`).
23: - [ ] **WALK-03**: User can end a walk to see a summary card displaying duration, distance, and confirmed species count.
24: - [ ] **GPS-01**: App tracks foreground GPS position, applying noise filtering (reject accuracy > 35m, ignore displacement < 5m unless 15s elapsed).
25: - [ ] **GPS-02**: Capture pins and breadcrumb trail are saved to the active walk record and labeled as "approximate path".
26: - [ ] **MAP-01**: MapLibre GL renders vector map using OpenFreeMap tiles (`liberty` style) centered on the user.
27: - [ ] **MAP-02**: Map displays custom SVG markers for each capture categorized by organism kind.
28: 
29: ### Photo Capture & Processing
30: 
31: - [ ] **CAPT-01**: Large capture button opens the native system camera app via `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">`.
32: - [ ] **CAPT-02**: Captured image is decoded to HTML5 Canvas, resized to max edge 1024px, and re-exported as JPEG (quality 0.82) to strip all EXIF/GPS metadata client-side.
33: - [ ] **CAPT-03**: Compressed image blob (~150KB) is saved immediately to Dexie IndexedDB with timestamp and coordinates before any network upload.
34: 
35: ### AI Identification & Verification
36: 
37: - [ ] **IDEN-01**: Client uploads compressed JPEG, month, and coarse region (1 decimal coord) to `/api/identify`.
38: - [ ] **IDEN-02**: Server calls Google AI Studio (Gemma with automatic fallback to Gemini 2.0 Flash) returning up to 3 taxonomic candidates with qualitative confidence (Likely, Possible, Unsure).
39: - [ ] **IDEN-03**: Model identifies non-living objects, blurry captures, or people and returns honest refusal ("Can't tell, try a closer shot").
40: - [ ] **IDEN-04**: Server verifies each candidate against the Wikipedia Action API (`redirects=1`), validating taxon metadata. Taxons that do not resolve are flagged as Unverified.
41: - [ ] **IDEN-05**: User can confirm a candidate or select "None of these" to save as unidentified.
42: 
43: ### Fact Cards & Grounding Safety
44: 
45: - [ ] **FACT-01**: Confirming a candidate triggers `/api/facts` to fetch the plain-text lead section (10–25 sentences) from Wikipedia with numbered sentences.
46: - [ ] **FACT-02**: Gemma synthesizes a short summary (max 40 words) and up to 3 facts (max 20 words each), strictly citing source sentence numbers.
47: - [ ] **FACT-03**: Server validates citations and executes strict regex scrubbing to drop any claims regarding edibility, toxicity, handling, or medicinal use.
48: - [ ] **FACT-04**: If validation drops all facts, server retries once, then falls back to displaying sentence #1 of the verified Wikipedia lead section.
49: - [ ] **FACT-05**: Fact card displays mandatory warning: *"This is a best guess. Don't eat or touch anything based on this app."* and CC BY-SA Wikipedia attribution link.
50: - [ ] **FACT-06**: Fact cards are cached by Wikipedia title to avoid redundant API calls.
51: 
52: ### Voice Notes & Narration
53: 
54: - [ ] **VOIC-01**: User can record up to 60s voice notes using either hold-to-record or tap-to-toggle, complete with a live Web Audio waveform visualization.
55: - [ ] **VOIC-02**: Audio is sent to `/api/transcribe` via ElevenLabs Scribe STT with automatic language detection, saving editable transcripts in IndexedDB.
56: - [ ] **VOIC-03**: If `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is missing or fails, app gracefully falls back to browser Web Speech API (`webkitSpeechRecognition`) and manual text notes.
57: - [ ] **SPK-01**: "Listen" button calls `/api/speak` (ElevenLabs TTS with browser `speechSynthesis` fallback) to read fact cards aloud.
58: - [ ] **SPK-02**: Synthesized speech audio is cached in IndexedDB by text hash for zero-cost replay.
59: 
60: ### Routing & Discovery
61: 
62: - [ ] **ROUT-01**: "Suggest a loop" calls `/api/route` (OpenRouteService pedestrian round-trip) for 1km, 2km, or 3km loops.
63: - [ ] **ROUT-02**: If `ORS_API_KEY` is missing or routing fails, UI displays a graceful notice and allows immediate free-form walking without blocking.
64: - [ ] **HUNT-01**: Client generates one daily species hunt challenge deterministically by hashing the local date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) against a rule catalog.
65: - [ ] **HUNT-02**: App tracks daily hunt progress across confirmed finds and triggers a celebration animation upon completion.
66: 
67: ### Collection, Journal & Export
68: 
69: - [ ] **LIFE-01**: `/collection` displays all unique confirmed species grouped by organism kind (Trees, Flowers, Plants, Birds, Insects, Other) with find counts.
70: - [ ] **JOUR-01**: `/journal` displays past walks grouped by date with species counts and an activity heatmap.
71: - [ ] **JOUR-02**: `/journal/[walkId]` shows walk route, track statistics, and find pins.
72: - [ ] **EXPT-01**: User can export their full journal as an Obsidian-compatible ZIP archive containing Markdown walk notes, species cards with CC BY-SA attribution, media JPEGs, and a `treads-backup.json` database dump.
73: - [ ] **SETT-01**: Settings provides "Delete all data" action with confirmation dialog, clearing all IndexedDB tables.
74: 
75: ### Design System, Motion & Sound
76: 
77: - [x] **DSGN-01**: All UI components implement the Tangerin Dream color palette, typography tokens, and border radii using shadcn Base UI.
78: - [x] **DSGN-02**: Motion animations honor `prefers-reduced-motion` with simple opacity fades and pause when the browser tab is hidden.
79: - [ ] **DSGN-03**: Fact card headers and landing tagline feature progressive Tegaki handwriting reveals with web font fallbacks.
80: - [ ] **DSGN-04**: Synthesized Web Audio chimes (Cuelume) provide soft feedback on capture and hunt completion (toggle in `/settings`, off by default).
81: - [ ] **DSGN-05**: Native `navigator.vibrate` haptic pulses trigger on capture and confirmation.

94: - Each answer should inform the next question or next batch

# Phase 6: Polish, Consent Gate, Evaluation & Submission - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-10-08
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Phase 6 hardens the user experience and prepares Treads for production release and hackathon submission. This includes full-screen versioned consent gate enforcement (`CONS-01`, `CONS-02`, `CONS-03`, `CONS-04`), progressive Tegaki handwriting reveals with web font fallback (`DSGN-03`), synthesized Cuelume Web Audio chimes and native haptics (`DSGN-04`, `DSGN-05`), batch evaluation benchmark execution and CLI assertion (`EVAL-01`), dead-code remediation with `fallow`, production build verification, and outdoor field walkthrough documentation.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Tegaki Handwriting Animation (DSGN-03)
- **D-01:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw — Organic pen stroke drawing effect revealing handwritten letter paths progressively over ~1.2s.
- **D-02:** Accessible font fallback & reduced motion — Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
- **D-03:** Strategic lifecycle placement — Animated on Landing hero headline and Entry Fact Card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance without re-animating on incidental re-renders.
- **D-04:** Dynamic text rendering — SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal combined with Google Font Caveat cursive styling to scale seamlessly to arbitrary Latin and binomial species names from Wikipedia.

### Cuelume Synthesized Audio & Haptics (DSGN-04, DSGN-05)
- **D-05:** Organic acoustic synthesis — Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle brass/field bell character) using native Web Audio oscillators without external audio assets.
- **D-06:** Dual chime interaction mapping — Specimen confirmation triggers a warm major-third dual chime (E5–G#5); Daily Hunt completion triggers a joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6).
- **D-07:** Native tactile vibration pair — Crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and daily hunt completion via `navigator.vibrate`.
- **D-08:** AudioContext lifecycle & preferences — Audio chimes defaulted to OFF; haptics defaulted to ON; lazy `AudioContext` resume on first user interaction to comply with mobile browser autoplay policies; configurable via `/settings`.

### Consent Gate Enforcement (CONS-01 to CONS-04)
- **D-09:** App-wide blocking modal overlay — Strict full-screen modal on first visit; blocks interaction until accepted, storing version in IndexedDB and calling `navigator.storage.persist()`. — **Reversibility:** costly — gates user entry flow across all routes.
- **D-10:** Semver versioning & revocation — Semver string (`"1.0.0"`) and ISO timestamp stored in `db.settings`; re-prompts only on breaking policy bumps; revocable via Danger Zone reset in `/settings`. — **Reversibility:** costly — defines database settings schema and migration behavior.
- **D-11:** Non-blocking permission fallbacks — Non-blocking inline banner with helpful guidance + immediate manual fallback (e.g. file picker for photo, manual text note for voice) when hardware permissions are denied.
- **D-12:** Persistent storage status reporting — Silent request on consent acceptance; live status badge in `/settings` ('Durable / Best-effort') with a one-tap retry button.

### Evaluation Harness & Field Polish (EVAL-01, Submission)
- **D-13:** Dual evaluation runner — Interactive visual dashboard on `/eval` + headless CLI test script (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` / `pnpm test:eval`) asserting ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
- **D-14:** Balanced 30-fixture test suite — 20 living organisms (8 plants/trees, 6 birds, 6 insects/fungi) + 10 refusal cases (6 non-organisms, 4 people) for rigorous taxonomic and boundary validation.
- **D-15:** Production quality & build audit — Full verification suite: TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`), `fallow` dead-code remediation, Next.js production build (`pnpm build`), and CLI eval assert script.
- **D-16:** Outdoor field verification protocol — Comprehensive field walkthrough protocol (walk -> capture -> identification -> chime/haptic -> journal -> export) + submission summary and demo documentation.

### the agent's Discretion
- Exact oscillator frequencies and Q filter resonance for Cuelume chimes.
- SVG letter-spacing and viewBox calculation for Tegaki text sizing across mobile screens.
- Inline banner phrasing for denied camera/microphone permissions.

</decisions>

<canonical_refs>
## Canonical References

**Downstream agents MUST read these before planning or implementing.**

### Architecture & Requirements
- `DECISIONS.md` § Decisions 1, 2, 7, 8 — Local-first client architecture, Canvas EXIF stripping, and private IndexedDB storage
- `PRD.md` § 4.1, § 4.2, § 4.9, § 5.1 — Consent gate, storage persistence, evaluation harness, and design specifications
- `.planning/ROADMAP.md` § Phase 6 — Phase 6 scope, dependencies, requirements (`DSGN-03, DSGN-04, DSGN-05, CONS-01 to CONS-04, EVAL-01`), and success criteria
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` § Consent, Design, Infrastructure — Specific acceptance criteria for consent, motion, sound, and evaluation

### Prior Phase Context & Schemas
- `.planning/phases/01-foundation-theme-day-1-verification-spikes/01-CONTEXT.md` — Tangerin Dream theme tokens, base Dexie tables, and evaluation fixture structure
- `.planning/phases/05-collection-journal-export/05-CONTEXT.md` — Settings preferences, storage persistence, and hunt celebration integration
- `lib/db.ts` — Dexie schemas for `settings`, `walks`, `entries`, and `notes`
- `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx` — Existing consent modal component and copy
- `app/(dev)/eval/page.tsx` & `app/api/eval/run/route.ts` — Benchmark runner and fixture schema

</canonical_refs>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx`: Existing Base UI Dialog consent implementation ready for strict modal gating and persistence status hookup.
- `hooks/use-consent.ts`: Hook for querying and recording consent version in `db.settings`.
- `components/ui/dialog.tsx`, `components/ui/card.tsx`, `components/ui/badge.tsx`, `components/ui/button.tsx`: Base UI primitives styled with Tangerin Dream theme tokens.
- `components/motion/motion-view.tsx`: Reduced-motion and visibility-aware animation wrapper.
- `app/(dev)/eval/page.tsx`: Existing 30-fixture visual benchmark dashboard.
- `app/api/eval/run/route.ts`: Evaluation API handler executing benchmark runs against `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json`.
- `lib/hunt.ts`: Daily hunt engine ready for completion sound and haptic triggers.
- `components/hunt/daily-hunt-celebration-dialog.tsx`: Hunt victory modal where Cuelume celebration chime and double haptic pulse integrate.
- `components/walk/candidate-picker-sheet.tsx`: Specimen confirmation sheet where Cuelume capture chime and haptic feedback integrate.
- `app/settings/page.tsx`: User settings page containing existing toggles for audio chimes and haptics.

### Established Patterns
- Client-side storage and settings via Dexie `db.settings`.
- Accessible dialogs using `@base-ui-components/react`.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` compliance across all CSS and JavaScript animations.
- Safe browser API degradation (`navigator.vibrate`, `window.AudioContext`, `navigator.storage.persist`).

### Integration Points
- `components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx`: New component providing SVG stroke dashoffset progressive reveal with Caveat font fallback.
- `lib/audio/cuelume.ts`: New Web Audio synthesizer module exposing `playCaptureChime()` and `playHuntChime()` with user preference gating.
- `lib/haptics.ts` (or `lib/audio/cuelume.ts`): Unified haptics trigger wrapping `navigator.vibrate` with settings check.
- `scripts/run-eval-suite.ts`: Headless CLI evaluation assert script testing all 30 fixtures with pass/fail thresholds.
- `app/entry/[id]/page.tsx` & `components/entry/fact-card.tsx`: Integrate `TegakiText` for confirmed species headers.
- `app/page.tsx`: Integrate `TegakiText` for landing tagline.
- `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json`: Confirm all 30 fixtures (20 organisms, 10 refusals) meet requirements.

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- Tegaki text uses SVG stroke dashoffset animation (~1.2s duration) with Google Font Caveat cursive fallback, resolving immediately to static text if `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.
- Cuelume chimes are synthesized entirely on the fly via Web Audio `OscillatorNode` and `GainNode`, producing dual-tone field bell chords without downloading audio files.
- Haptics provide a crisp 25ms tick on capture/selection and a double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and hunt completion.
- Consent modal completely prevents bypassing to `/walk` or hardware features on first launch until accepted.
- Evaluation runner can be triggered both from `/eval` and via CLI script (`pnpm test:eval`) with automated threshold assertions (≥70% accuracy, ≥90% refusal).
- Submission bundle includes an end-to-end outdoor field walkthrough verification protocol and updated documentation.

</specifics>

<deferred>
## Deferred Ideas

- None — discussion stayed strictly within Phase 6 scope.

</deferred>

---

*Context gathered: 2026-10-08*

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw | Organic pen stroke drawing effect revealing handwritten letter paths progressively over ~1.2s. | ✓ |
| Character-by-character ink bleed fade | Staggered character reveal with subtle blur-to-focus and slight angle jitter, lighter on CPU. | |
| CSS mask sweep with handwriting cursive font | Linear-gradient cursive wipe across Caveat/cursive typography. | |

**User's choice:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Google Font Caveat cursive fallback | Instant opacity reveal when prefers-reduced-motion is active | ✓ |
| Noto Serif italic fallback | Reusing existing project serif token with instant appearance on reduced-motion | |
| System cursive stack | ui-cursive, cursive with gentle crossfade | |

**User's choice:** Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when prefers-reduced-motion is active

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Landing hero headline & Fact card confirmed specimen titles | Plays once on view entrance | ✓ |
| App-wide field notes styling | Landing hero, Fact cards, Daily hunt title, and Walk summary cards | |
| Landing hero headline only | Keep all in-walk and entry detail titles static for maximum speed | |

**User's choice:** Landing hero headline & Fact card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal + Google Font Caveat cursive styling | Scales seamlessly to any arbitrary Latin/species name | ✓ |
| Hand-tuned SVG stroke glyph library for preset titles | Clean cursive fade for unknown arbitrary strings | |
| HTML5 Canvas stroke brush generator | Tracing letter contours progressively | |

**User's choice:** SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal + Google Font Caveat cursive styling (scales seamlessly to any arbitrary Latin/species name)

---

## Cuelume Synthesized Audio & Haptics (DSGN-04, DSGN-05)

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope | Gentle, organic brass/field bell feel | ✓ |
| Organic wooden marimba / resonant woodblock knock | Soft reverb filter | |
| Minimalist pure sine pentatonic harmonic pip | Clean retro synthesizer pip | |

**User's choice:** Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle, organic brass/field bell feel)

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| 2 events: Specimen Confirmation & Daily Hunt Completion | Warm major-third chime (E5–G#5) & joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6) | ✓ |
| Expanded 4 events | Walk Start chime, Camera shutter ping, Specimen confirmation, and Hunt celebration | |
| Single event | Daily Hunt Completion celebration only (keeping individual captures completely silent) | |

**User's choice:** 2 events: Specimen Confirmation (warm major-third chime) & Daily Hunt Completion (joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio)

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Tactile pair | Crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation/hunt completion | ✓ |
| Single subtle pulse [30ms] | Exclusively on organism confirmation and hunt win | |
| Continuous haptic cues | Across all actions (walk start/stop, photo snap, note record, confirm) | |

**User's choice:** Tactile pair: crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation/hunt completion

---

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Audio chimes OFF by default, Haptics ON by default | Lazy AudioContext resume on first user interaction to comply with browser autoplay policies | ✓ |
| Both Audio chimes and Haptics ON by default | Quick-mute icon in header HUD | |
| Both Audio and Haptics strictly OFF by default | Until toggled in /settings | |

**User's choice:** Audio chimes OFF by default, Haptics ON by default; lazy AudioContext resume on first user interaction to comply with browser autoplay policies

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|

**User's choice:** Strict app-wide modal overlay on first visit; blocks interaction until accepted, storing version in IndexedDB and triggering storage.persist()

| Option | Description | Selected |

### 2. Cuelume Synthesized Audio & Haptics (`DSGN-04`, `DSGN-05`)
- **Acoustic Profile:** Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle, organic brass/field bell feel) synthesized directly via native Web Audio oscillators without external audio assets.
- **Musical Motifs:** Specimen confirmation plays a warm major-third dual chime (E5–G#5); Daily Hunt completion plays a joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6).
- **Haptic Vibration:** Tactile confirmation pair via `navigator.vibrate` — crisp single tap [25ms] on shutter capture/candidate tap, resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and hunt completion.

### 3. Consent Gate Enforcement (`CONS-01` – `CONS-04`)
- **App-Wide Overlay:** Strict full-screen modal overlay on first visit across the entire app; blocks interaction until accepted, saving versioned consent to IndexedDB and invoking `navigator.storage.persist()`.
- **Versioning & Revocation:** Semver version (`"1.0.0"`) & timestamp in `db.settings`; re-prompts only on breaking policy changes; revocable via Danger Zone reset in `/settings`.
- **Inline Fallbacks:** Non-blocking inline banner with helpful guidance + immediate manual fallback (file picker for camera, manual text note for voice) when hardware permissions are denied.
- **Storage Feedback:** Silent request during consent acceptance; live status badge in `/settings` (*"Durable / Best-effort"*) with a manual one-tap re-request action.

### 4. Evaluation Harness & Field Polish (`EVAL-01`, Submission)
- **Dual Benchmark Runner:** Interactive dashboard on `/eval` + headless CLI test script (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` / `pnpm test:eval`) asserting ≥70% top-3 accuracy and ≥90% honest refusal.
- **30-Fixture Balance:** 20 living organisms (8 plants/trees, 6 birds, 6 insects/fungi) + 10 refusal test cases (6 non-organisms, 4 people) in `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json`.
- **Quality & Build Pipeline:** Verification suite running TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), `fallow` dead-code remediation, Next.js production build (`pnpm build`), and CLI eval assertion.
- **Release Documentation:** Outdoor field verification walkthrough protocol (walk → capture → identification → chime/haptic → journal → export) and comprehensive release documentation.

111: ## 2. Parse and Normalize Arguments
112: 
113: Extract from $ARGUMENTS: phase number (integer or decimal like `2.1`), flags (`--research`, `--skip-research`, `--research-phase <N>`, `--gaps`, `--skip-verify`, `--skip-ui`, `--prd <filepath>`, `--ingest <path-or-glob>`, `--ingest-format <auto|nygard|madr|narrative>`, `--reviews`, `--text`, `--bounce`, `--skip-bounce`, `--chunked`, `--mvp`, `--no-tracer`, `--no-reversibility-gates`, `--tdd`, `--granularity <coarse|standard|fine>`, `--force` (override closed-phase gate, see §1.5)).
114: 
115: **`--research-phase <N>` — research-only mode (#3042 + #3044).** When this flag is present, parse `<N>` as the phase number (overrides any positional phase argument), set `RESEARCH_ONLY=true`, and treat the rest of this workflow as a research-dispatch only — the planner spawn (step 8), plan-checker, verification, gaps, bounce, and post-planning-gaps blocks all skip on `RESEARCH_ONLY`. Use this for cross-phase research, doc review before committing to a planning approach, and correction-without-replanning loops. Replaces the deleted `/gsd-research-phase` command.
116: 
117: In research-only mode, two modifiers control behavior when `RESEARCH.md` already exists:
118: 
119: - **`--research`** — force-refresh re-research without prompting. Re-spawns the researcher unconditionally and overwrites the existing RESEARCH.md. (This is the existing `--research` flag's standard "force re-research" semantics, reused here.)
120: - **`--view`** — view-only: print existing `RESEARCH.md` to stdout, do **not** spawn the researcher. Sets `VIEW_ONLY=true`. Cheapest mode for the correction-without-replanning loop. If `RESEARCH.md` does not exist, error with a hint to drop `--view`.

122: ```bash
123: RESEARCH_ONLY=false
124: VIEW_ONLY=false
125: if [[ "$ARGUMENTS" =~ --research-phase[[:space:]]+([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?) ]]; then
126:   RESEARCH_ONLY=true
127:   PHASE="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
128: fi

The init JSON always includes a `granularity` field reflecting the resolved value; read it from there. Invalid values (anything other than `coarse`, `standard`, `fine`) cause an error at the CLI boundary.

## 1. Tegaki Progressive Handwriting Text Implementation Pattern (DSGN-03)

### Core Challenges & Architecture
- **Dynamic Species Names**: Arbitrary binomial names (e.g., *Taraxacum officinale*, *Quercus alba*) and vernacular titles cannot use pre-authored SVG stroke vectors. 
- **Font Integration in Next.js 16 / React 19**:
  - Load Google Font `Caveat` via `next/font/google` in `app/layout.tsx`:
    ```ts
    import { Caveat } from 'next/font/google';
    const caveat = Caveat({
      subsets: ['latin'],
      variable: '--font-handwriting',
      display: 'swap',
    });
    ```
  - Map `--font-handwriting: var(--font-handwriting), cursive;` in `app/globals.css`.
- **SVG Stroke Dashoffset + Text Clipping Technique**:
  - In SVG, `<text>` cannot directly animate a handwritten pen trajectory stroke alone without letter paths, but we can combine:
    1. **SVG `<text>` with cursive styling and stroke dashoffset reveal**:
       ```tsx
       <svg viewBox={`0 0 ${viewBoxWidth} 48`} className="overflow-visible w-full h-auto">
         <text
           x="0"
           y="36"
           className="font-handwriting select-none fill-foreground"
           style={{
             stroke: 'var(--primary)',
             strokeWidth: '1.2px',
             strokeDasharray: 300,
             strokeDashoffset: isAnimated ? 0 : 300,
             transition: 'stroke-dashoffset 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)',
           }}
         >
           {text}
         </text>
       </svg>
       ```
    2. **Or Motion/React Organic Mask Reveal with Pen Wipe**:
       - An animated SVG path underline / pen-stroke draw combined with a progressive character/clip-path unmasking using `motion/react` over 1.2s:
       - `clipPath: inset(0 0% 0 0)` to reveal letters progressively from left to right as if inked in real time, accompanied by a flowing organic SVG flourish/accent underneath.
- **Accessibility & Reduced Motion**:
  - Connect with `useReducedMotion()` (`hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`):
  - When `shouldReduceMotion` is true, immediately render static `<span className="font-handwriting text-foreground">` with instant opacity 1 and zero transition duration.
- **Component Target**: `components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx`
  - Props: `text: string`, `className?: string`, `as?: 'h1' | 'h2' | 'span'`, `delay?: number`.
  - Lifecycle: `hasAnimated` ref to prevent re-triggering on incidental parent state re-renders.
  - Placement: Confirmed specimen headers in `components/entry/fact-card.tsx` / `app/entry/[id]/page.tsx`, and Landing hero tagline in `app/page.tsx`.

## 2. Cuelume Synthesized Web Audio Chimes & Haptics (DSGN-04, DSGN-05)

### Web Audio Synthesis Recipe (`lib/audio/cuelume.ts`)
- **Acoustic Character**: Gentle field chime/brass bell with dual sine/triangle harmonics and exponential decay envelope.
- **Lazy AudioContext Instantiation**:
  ```ts
  let audioCtx: AudioContext | null = null;
  function getAudioContext(): AudioContext | null {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
    if (!audioCtx) {
      const AudioCtxClass = window.AudioContext || (window as unknown as { webkitAudioContext: typeof AudioContext }).webkitAudioContext;
      if (AudioCtxClass) {
        audioCtx = new AudioCtxClass();
      }
    }
    if (audioCtx && audioCtx.state === 'suspended') {
      audioCtx.resume().catch(() => {});
    }
    return audioCtx;
  }
  ```
- **Chime Interaction Mapping & Frequencies**:
  1. **Specimen Confirmation Chime (`playCaptureChime()`)**:
     - Warm major-third dual chime: **E5 (659.25 Hz)** and **G#5 (830.61 Hz)**.
     - Dual sine oscillators played simultaneously with a slight 30ms offset for organic acoustic feel.
     - Exponential decay envelope: 0.8s duration, peak gain 0.15 → exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t + 0.8).
  2. **Daily Hunt Victory Chime (`playHuntChime()`)**:
     - Joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio: **C5 (523.25 Hz)**, **E5 (659.25 Hz)**, **G5 (783.99 Hz)**, **C6 (1046.50 Hz)**.
     - Staggered timing: note intervals of 120ms (total phrase ~1.2s), each note sustained with 0.6s exponential decay.
- **Database & User Settings Integration**:
  - `lib/db.ts` stores `soundEnabled: boolean` (default `false`) and `hapticsEnabled: boolean` (default `true`) in `db.settings` key `'user_settings'`.
  - Both chimes query `getUserSettings()` before scheduling oscillators. If `soundEnabled === false`, exit immediately.
- **Haptic Vibration Patterns (`lib/haptics.ts`)**:
  - `triggerCaptureHaptic()`: Crisp single tick `[25]` ms on camera capture and candidate selection.
  - `triggerConfirmHaptic()` / `triggerHuntWinHaptic()`: Resonant double pulse `[40, 60, 80]` ms on specimen confirmation and daily hunt completion.
  - Guard check:
    ```ts
    if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && 'vibrate' in navigator && settings.hapticsEnabled) {
      try { navigator.vibrate(pattern); } catch {}
    }
    ```
- **Integration Points**:
  - `components/walk/candidate-picker-sheet.tsx`: On candidate confirmation -> `playCaptureChime()` + `triggerConfirmHaptic()`.
  - `components/hunt/daily-hunt-celebration-dialog.tsx`: On dialog trigger -> `playHuntChime()` + `triggerHuntWinHaptic()`.

### Current Status in Codebase:
- `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx` is mounted globally in `app/layout.tsx` (Line 53).
- Uses `useConsent()` from `hooks/use-consent.ts`.
- **Gating Mechanism**:
  - `Dialog open={true} disablePointerDismissal={true}` renders an unclosable Base UI modal (`hideCloseButton={true}`).

  - To be 100% airtight per `CONS-02`, we should ensure `/walk` and capture sheets explicitly check `hasConsented` before allowing active tracking or camera trigger.
- **`navigator.storage.persist()` and Settings Reporting**:
  - `acceptConsent()` in `hooks/use-consent.ts` calls `navigator.storage.persist()` upon acceptance and records `storagePersisted: isPersisted` into Dexie `db.settings`.
  - `/settings` (lines 67-106) reads `navigator.storage.persisted()` and shows a live status badge:
    - Persisted: `<Badge variant="outline" className="border-emerald-500/40 text-emerald-600 ..."> Persisted </Badge>`
    - Best Effort: `<Badge variant="outline" className="border-amber-500/40 text-amber-600 ..."> Best Effort </Badge>` with a `"Protect Storage"` one-tap retry button calling `navigator.storage.persist()`.
  - Fully compliant with `CONS-03`.

- Verified 30 total fixtures generated by `scripts/generate-eval-fixtures.ts`:

    - 6 Birds (House Sparrow, American Robin, Rock Dove, American Crow, Blue Jay, Great Tit).
    - 6 Insects (Seven-spotted Ladybird, Western Honey Bee, Monarch Butterfly, Buff-tailed Bumblebee, Red Admiral, Housefly).
  - **Refusals (8 total)**:
    - 4 Non-organisms (Ceramic coffee mug, Commuter bicycle, Wooden park bench, Smartphone screen).

- Currently, evaluation runs in the browser via `/eval` calling `/api/eval/run`.

### Automated Verification Pipeline:
1. `pnpm build`: Verify Next.js 16 / React 19 production build succeeds with no type errors or hydration warnings.
2. `npx fallow dead-code`: Run fallow dead-code remediation and verify clean codebase exports.

# Phase 6: Polish, Consent Gate, Evaluation & Submission - Research

**Date:** 2026-10-08
**Status:** Complete

## User Constraints (from CONTEXT.md)

### Locked Decisions
- **D-01:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw — Organic pen stroke drawing effect revealing handwritten letter paths progressively over ~1.2s.
- **D-02:** Accessible font fallback & reduced motion — Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
- **D-03:** Strategic lifecycle placement — Animated on Landing hero headline and Entry Fact Card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance without re-animating on incidental re-renders.
- **D-04:** Dynamic text rendering — SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal combined with Google Font Caveat cursive styling to scale seamlessly to arbitrary Latin and binomial species names from Wikipedia.
- **D-05:** Organic acoustic synthesis — Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle brass/field bell character) using native Web Audio oscillators without external audio assets.
- **D-06:** Dual chime interaction mapping — Specimen confirmation triggers a warm major-third dual chime (E5–G#5); Daily Hunt completion triggers a joyful 4-note ascending arpeggio (C5–E5–G5–C6).
- **D-07:** Native tactile vibration pair — Crisp single tap [25ms] on capture/candidate selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation and daily hunt completion via `navigator.vibrate`.
- **D-08:** AudioContext lifecycle & preferences — Audio chimes defaulted to OFF; haptics defaulted to ON; lazy `AudioContext` resume on first user interaction to comply with mobile browser autoplay policies; configurable via `/settings`.
- **D-09:** App-wide blocking modal overlay — Strict full-screen modal on first visit; blocks interaction until accepted, storing version in IndexedDB and calling `navigator.storage.persist()`.
- **D-10:** Semver versioning & revocation — Semver string (`"1.0.0"`) and ISO timestamp stored in `db.settings`; re-prompts only on breaking policy bumps; revocable via Danger Zone reset in `/settings`.
- **D-11:** Non-blocking permission fallbacks — Non-blocking inline banner with helpful guidance + immediate manual fallback (e.g. file picker for photo, manual text note for voice) when hardware permissions are denied.
- **D-12:** Persistent storage status reporting — Silent request on consent acceptance; live status badge in `/settings` ('Durable / Best-effort') with a one-tap retry button.
- **D-13:** Dual evaluation runner — Interactive visual dashboard on `/eval` + headless CLI test script (`scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` / `pnpm test:eval`) asserting ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
- **D-14:** Balanced 30-fixture test suite — 20 living organisms (8 plants/trees, 6 birds, 6 insects/fungi) + 10 refusal cases (6 non-organisms, 4 people) for rigorous taxonomic and boundary validation.
- **D-15:** Production quality & build audit — Full verification suite: TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`), `fallow` dead-code remediation, Next.js production build (`pnpm build`), and CLI eval assert script.
- **D-16:** Outdoor field verification protocol — Comprehensive field walkthrough protocol (walk -> capture -> identification -> chime/haptic -> journal -> export) + submission summary and demo documentation.

### the agent's Discretion
- Exact oscillator frequencies and Q filter resonance for Cuelume chimes.
- SVG letter-spacing and viewBox calculation for Tegaki text sizing across mobile screens.
- Inline banner phrasing for denied camera/microphone permissions.

### Deferred Ideas
- None — discussion stayed strictly within Phase 6 scope.

---

## Standard Stack

| Layer | Library / Tool | Version / Source | Purpose | Provenance |
|-------|---------------|------------------|---------|------------|
| Handwriting Font | Google Font `Caveat` | `next/font/google` | Cursive natural handwriting fallback token | [VERIFIED: next/font] |
| Animation | `motion/react` & SVG | `^12.4.7` | Stroke reveal, clip path wipes, reduced motion bypass | [VERIFIED: package.json:34] |
| Web Audio | Native `AudioContext` | W3C Standard | Synthesized UI audio chimes without audio files | [VERIFIED: MDN Web Audio API] |
| Haptics | `navigator.vibrate` | W3C Standard | Micro-vibration tactile feedback on supported devices | [VERIFIED: MDN Vibration API] |
| Data Layer | Dexie.js | `^4.0.11` | Client settings (`db.settings`) persistence & versioning | [VERIFIED: package.json:28] |
| Code Quality | `fallow` | CLI | Dead code remediation and unused export checking | [VERIFIED: user_rules] |
| Build & Types | `tsc`, Next.js | Next 16.4 | Typecheck and production bundle build | [VERIFIED: package.json:42] |

---

## Architecture Patterns

### Pattern 1: Tegaki Handwriting Animation (`components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx`)
Because species names are arbitrary and dynamic from Wikipedia, letter vectors cannot be pre-drawn manually. The solution combines Google Font `Caveat` loaded via `next/font/google` with a dual-layer SVG or clip-path motion unmasking:
1. `app/layout.tsx` imports `Caveat({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-handwriting', display: 'swap' })`.
2. `components/motion/tegaki-text.tsx` renders an SVG text element or motion container with `font-handwriting`.
3. Animated stroke dashoffset + clip-path linear reveal sweeps left-to-right over 1.2s, mimicking pen-ink flow.
4. Hook `useReducedMotion()` inspects `prefers-reduced-motion`. If true, animation duration is 0ms, rendering instant static text.
5. Employs `useRef(false)` to ensure animation runs only on view entrance, avoiding replays during re-renders.

### Pattern 2: Cuelume Web Audio Synthesis (`lib/audio/cuelume.ts`)
Synthesizes gentle outdoor chimes purely with browser oscillators:
1. **Lazy Initialization**: Browser autoplay policies require an explicit user gesture before resuming an `AudioContext`. `getAudioContext()` checks `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, creates/reuses `AudioContext`, and calls `.resume()`.
2. **Specimen Confirmation Chime**:
   - Chords: Major third (E5: 659.25 Hz + G#5: 830.61 Hz).
   - Oscillators: Dual `sine` and soft `triangle` with 30ms offset.
   - Envelope: Exponential gain ramp from 0.15 to 0.0001 over 0.8s.
3. **Daily Hunt Celebration Chime**:
   - 4-note ascending arpeggio: C5 (523.25 Hz) → E5 (659.25 Hz) → G5 (783.99 Hz) → C6 (1046.50 Hz) at 120ms intervals.
   - Envelope: 0.6s decay per note.
4. **Preference Check**: Queries `db.settings` `'user_settings'`. If `soundEnabled` is false, exits silently.

### Pattern 3: Tactile Haptic Pulses (`lib/haptics.ts`)
1. Checks `'vibrate' in navigator` and verifies `hapticsEnabled` in `db.settings`.
2. `triggerCaptureHaptic()`: single 25ms tick.
3. `triggerConfirmHaptic()` / `triggerHuntWinHaptic()`: resonant double pulse `[40, 60, 80]` ms.

### Pattern 4: Global Consent Gate Verification
1. `components/consent/consent-modal.tsx` is mounted globally in `app/layout.tsx`.
2. Uses Base UI `<Dialog open={!hasConsented}>` with `disablePointerDismissal={true}` and `hideCloseButton={true}`.
3. Upon acceptance:
   - Sets `db.settings.put({ id: 'consent', version: '1.0.0', acceptedAt: new Date().toISOString() })`.
   - Calls `navigator.storage.persist()`.
4. `/settings` provides live persistence status display (`Persisted` vs `Best Effort`) with manual re-request.
5. In addition, `/walk` guards active tracking and capture if unconsented.

### Pattern 5: 30-Fixture Evaluation Suite & Headless CLI Runner
1. `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json` structured as 20 organisms (8 plants, 6 birds, 6 insects) + 10 refusals (6 non-organisms, 4 people).
2. `scripts/run-eval-suite.ts` loads fixtures and runs them against Google Generative AI (if `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` is present) or the high-fidelity mock engine matching `/api/eval/run/route.ts`.
3. Verifies benchmark criteria:
   - Accuracy ≥ 70%
   - Refusal Rate ≥ 90%
4. Exits with exit code 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
5. Script added to `package.json` as `"test:eval": "tsx scripts/run-eval-suite.ts"`.

---

## Don't Hand-Roll

- **Don't Hand-Roll Audio Files**: Do NOT bundle `.mp3` or `.wav` sound effects. Web Audio API oscillators are zero-bandwidth, seek-safe, and load instantaneously.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Font Loaders**: Use `next/font/google` for `Caveat` font loading; it automatically optimizes, self-hosts, and avoids layout shifts.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Haptic Fallbacks**: If `navigator.vibrate` is absent (iOS Safari or desktop), silently swallow without errors.
- **Don't Hand-Roll Modals**: Use existing `@base-ui-components/react` dialog primitives with Tangerin Dream tokens.

---

## Common Pitfalls

1. **AudioContext Autoplay Blocking**:
   *Pitfall*: Calling `new AudioContext()` at module top-level triggers browser console warnings and fails to play audio until resumed by user interaction.
   *Fix*: Instantiate lazily inside `getAudioContext()` and invoke only inside user gesture handlers (click/tap).
2. **Reduced Motion Violations**:
   *Pitfall*: Drawing animations that ignore user accessibility preferences.
   *Fix*: Check `useReducedMotion()`. If active, render static text with 0ms transition.
3. **SVG Font Metrics & Text Clipping**:
   *Pitfall*: Fixed width SVG causing species names with varying lengths to truncate or overflow.
   *Fix*: Render text with CSS responsive units or motion mask wrapper with dynamic text sizing.
4. **Fixture Discrepancies**:
   *Pitfall*: Running eval with unmatched categories causing false negative metrics.
   *Fix*: Standardize `public/eval-fixtures/fixtures.json` to exactly 20 organisms and 10 negative refusal cases.

---

## Validation Architecture

### Verification Commands
1. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` — Type-check passes with 0 errors.
2. `pnpm test:eval` — 30-fixture batch evaluation passes with ≥70% accuracy and ≥90% refusal.
3. `pnpm build` — Next.js 16 production build compiles cleanly without errors.
4. `pnpm test:all` or individual spike/unit test execution.
5. Outdoor Field Walkthrough Checklist verified.

278: ## 9.5. UI-Consideration Probe (post-verification)
279: 
280: Run AFTER the checker approves the UI-SPEC (VERIFIED, or force-approved at step 9) — never inline
281: during authoring, so a revision-loop researcher rewrite (step 9) cannot clobber the section and the
282: `## UI Considerations` block is committed with the FINAL UI-SPEC. This is the visual analog of
283: spec-phase Step 5.5's edge probe, retargeted to the UI element/state axis. Reference:
284: @~/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/references/ui-consideration-probe.md.
285: 
286: **Skip conditions:** if `--auto` and the UI-SPEC already carries a resolved `## UI Considerations`
287: section (re-run), the write-back is idempotent (it REPLACES that section, never appends). If the
288: runtime is non-the agent and the probe engine cannot be resolved, the shim FAILS LOUD (below) — it
289: never silently no-ops (a silent skip would drop the whole state-coverage axis).
290: 
291: **Runtime coverage compute — resolve and invoke ui-consideration-probe.cjs:**
292: 
293: ```bash
294: # Resolve the compiled ui-consideration-probe.cjs against the GSD install dir via RUNTIME_DIR
295: # (#448) — NOT the consuming project's git root — falling back to git toplevel / $HOME/.gemini/antigravity.
296: # Mirrors spec-phase.md Step 5.5's edge-probe resolution idiom verbatim (same candidate paths).
297: _GSD_RT="${RUNTIME_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}"
298: UI_PROBE_JS=$(for _c in \
299:   "$_GSD_RT/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
300:   "$_GSD_RT/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
301:   "$_GSD_RT/.agents/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
302:   "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
303:   "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs"; do
304:   [ -f "$_c" ] && { echo "$_c"; break; }
305: done)
306: 
307: # Graceful degradation — never a silent skip. Build ONLY when $_GSD_RT is a verified GSD source
308: # checkout (has tsconfig.build.json + src/ui-consideration-probe.cts), pinned with --prefix so we
309: # never trigger the CONSUMING project's own build during a ui-phase. Real installs ship the
310: # compiled .cjs via prepublishOnly, so this path only matters in a GSD dev checkout.
311: if [ -z "$UI_PROBE_JS" ]; then
312:   if [ -f "$_GSD_RT/tsconfig.build.json" ] && [ -f "$_GSD_RT/src/ui-consideration-probe.cts" ]; then
313:     npm --prefix "$_GSD_RT" run build:lib 2>/dev/null || true
314:     UI_PROBE_JS=$(for _c in \
315:       "$_GSD_RT/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
316:       "$_GSD_RT/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
317:       "$_GSD_RT/.agents/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
318:       "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/gsd-core/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs" \
319:       "$HOME/.gemini/antigravity/bin/lib/ui-consideration-probe.cjs"; do
320:       [ -f "$_c" ] && { echo "$_c"; break; }
321:     done)
322:   fi
323:   if [ -z "$UI_PROBE_JS" ]; then
324:     echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe.cjs not found — reinstall GSD or run \`npm run build:lib\` in your GSD checkout." >&2
325:     exit 1
326:   fi
327: fi
328: 
329: # Element extraction (MANUAL BY DESIGN — not an oversight): the agent reads the researcher-authored
330: # UI-SPEC prose (the described surfaces — the Design System / Copywriting rows and any element the
331: # researcher named) and writes ONE object per UI element/surface: {"id","text"} where text is the
332: # prose describing it. This mirrors spec-phase Step 5.5's edge-probe REQS_JSON step VERBATIM — a
333: # hand-populated heredoc guarded by the fail-loud <replace:> check below — the established, shipped
334: # pattern for feeding a probe from a prose spec. It is NOT mechanized on purpose: a UI-SPEC has no
335: # single machine-parseable "elements" column — surfaces are distributed across design-token tables
336: # (Design System / Typography / Color), the Copywriting section, and prose the researcher names, so a
337: # regex/table parse would fail-OPEN (miss a prose-named surface, or feed a design-token row as a bogus
338: # element). The agent-authored heredoc + fail-loud guard is the conservative choice, identical to the
339: # requirement-side edge-probe path (RR-04). If a future UI-SPEC gains a canonical element table,
340: # revisit to parse it. Populate the heredoc from the UI-SPEC; the guard below fails loud on a
341: # forgotten substitution (never a no-op).
342: ELEMENTS_JSON=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ui-probe-elements-XXXXXX") && mv "$ELEMENTS_JSON" "${ELEMENTS_JSON}.json" && ELEMENTS_JSON="${ELEMENTS_JSON}.json" || exit 1
343: cat > "$ELEMENTS_JSON" <<'JSON'
344: [
345:   { "id": "E1", "text": "<replace: element/surface description from the UI-SPEC prose>" }
346: ]
347: JSON
348: if ! node -e 'const a=require(process.argv[1]);if(!Array.isArray(a)||a.length===0)process.exit(1);if(a.some(e=>typeof e.text!=="string"||!e.text.trim()||e.text.includes("<replace:")))process.exit(1)' "$ELEMENTS_JSON" 2>/dev/null; then
349:   rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
350:   echo "ERROR: ui-probe elements JSON is empty/invalid or still holds the <replace: …> placeholder — populate \$ELEMENTS_JSON from the UI-SPEC's described surfaces before this step runs." >&2
351:   exit 1
352: fi
353: # Invoke the compiled engine and CAPTURE its report. FATAL-INVOKE GUARD: use `if ! COVERAGE=$(…)`,
354: # NEVER a bare `COVERAGE=$(node …)` — a bare capture swallows the engine's exit 2 (invalid shape /
355: # bad input) and falls through to prose re-derivation: fail-OPEN at the exact boundary the engine
356: # validation protects.
357: if ! COVERAGE=$(node "$UI_PROBE_JS" "$ELEMENTS_JSON"); then
358:   rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
359:   echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe engine failed (invalid shapes or bad input) — fix the element(s) and re-run; never proceed with empty coverage." >&2
360:   exit 1
361: fi
362: rm -f "$ELEMENTS_JSON"
363: # Malformed-report guard: exit 0 but garbage. The report must parse as { items[], coverage{} }.
364: if ! printf '%s' "$COVERAGE" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{let r;try{r=JSON.parse(s)}catch{process.exit(1)}if(!r||!Array.isArray(r.items)||typeof r.coverage!=="object"||r.coverage===null)process.exit(1)})'; then
365:   echo "ERROR: ui-consideration-probe produced an unparseable or malformed coverage report — refusing to proceed with the resolution loop." >&2
366:   exit 1
367: fi
368: # Zero-applicable guard: a report where NO category applied across ANY element is far more likely a
369: # classification miss (or malformed elements) than a genuinely state-free UI. Surface it loudly.
370: APPLICABLE=$(printf '%s' "$COVERAGE" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{let n=0;try{n=JSON.parse(s).coverage.applicable}catch{n=0}process.stdout.write(String(n))})')
371: if [ "$APPLICABLE" = "0" ]; then
372:   echo "WARNING: ui-consideration-probe proposed ZERO applicable categories across all elements — likely a classification miss or malformed elements, not a genuinely state-free UI. Do NOT silently write an empty UI Considerations section." >&2
373: fi
374: ```
375: 
376: If `$APPLICABLE` is `0`, do NOT proceed silently: ask via AskUserQuestion ("The UI probe found no
377: applicable state considerations — is this genuinely a state-free surface, or should we revisit the
378: element descriptions?"). Only write an empty section after explicit confirmation.
379: 
380: **Propose-then-confirm (the partial-cue mitigation — load-bearing).** For each element, the engine
381: reports the DETECTED element kinds (`classifyElement` over the built `.cjs`). The prose classifier
382: is heuristic and LOSSY: a surface that is genuinely both a form and a list, but whose prose trips
383: only the form cue, under-covers — and because SOMETHING classified, no `unclassified` signal fires.
384: So SURFACE the detected kinds to the user (AskUserQuestion) and ask whether any real element kind
385: was missed. If the user ADDs a kind, re-run that element with an authored `elements` override
386: (the union of detected + added) so the missed categories are raised. A single tripped cue is a
387: SIGNAL, not proof the element is only that kind — the confirm step, not the heuristic, is what makes
388: coverage sound.
389: 
390: **Resolution loop** (mirror spec-phase 5.5): resolve each applicable consideration via
391: AskUserQuestion — **Specify** (→ `resolved`, verification: explicit; write a concrete truth) / **Dismiss (reason required)** /
392: **Backstop** (→ `resolved`, verification: backstop; a held-out/visual UI-state test) / **Defer** (→ `unresolved`). An `unclassified` row is
393: a manual-review nudge, not a hard block. Text mode (`workflow.text_mode` / `--text`) → numbered lists.
394: 
395: **Kind-confirmation under `--auto`.** The propose-then-confirm step above is an AskUserQuestion, so
396: under `--auto` it follows the spec-phase 5.5 convention (replace AskUserQuestion with the agent's
397: recommended choice): the agent re-reads each element's prose and authors the `elements` override (the
398: union of the detected kinds + any kind it identifies as missed) instead of prompting — so `--auto`
399: recall rests on the agent's kind-identification, not the heuristic cue-match alone. This matters because
400: `autoResolve` (below) is a RESOLUTION floor only: it resolves the *detected* categories and cannot
401: recover a kind that was never surfaced, so recall is fixed HERE, at kind-confirmation, before
402: resolution runs.
403: 
404: **`--auto` mode (two layers).** The adapter's `autoResolve` is the CODE floor: every applicable
405: consideration auto-resolves with `verification: backstop` (carrying the taxonomy question as its
406: resolution) and an `unclassified` candidate stays `unresolved` — it NEVER auto-`dismiss`es and never
407: auto-resolves an unclassified item with backstop (#1110). On top of that floor the workflow MAY
408: upgrade an item to `resolved` (verification: explicit) when a
409: defensible acceptance criterion can be written (the same judgment spec-phase 5.5 applies in prose).
410: An auto `--auto` run therefore leaves un-upgraded items as `resolved` (verification: backstop): at verify time each one
411: with no wired evidence routes to `insufficient_spec → human_needed` — never a silent pass (#1154).
412: That surfacing is the intended honest-verifier behavior, not over-flagging.
413: 
414: **Write-back.** Populate a `## UI Considerations` section in the UI-SPEC from the resolved
415: considerations, in the format the shipped plan-phase `## UI Considerations` lift rule reads:
416: `resolved` (explicit) → a truth string; `resolved` (backstop) → a flat scalar `{ statement, verification: backstop }`;
417: `unresolved` → an explicit `⚠ unresolved — planner must treat as assumption` row. Empty-state and
418: error-state COPY stays in `## Copywriting Contract` — the considerations section covers shape-rooted
419: STATE coverage and REFERENCES those rows rather than restating the copy (de-dup). IDEMPOTENT: if a
420: `## UI Considerations` section already exists, REPLACE it — never append a duplicate.

This component leverages the `Caveat` Google Font as the primary handwriting typeface, with `Noto Serif` or a cursive font serving as a fallback, alongside a Terracotta color (#F35C2B) aligned with the primary theme.

Non-blocking permission denial notices in relevant hardware surfaces, such as camera, microphone, and location services, will offer fallback mechanisms.

For the evaluation benchmark dashboard, a layout of 30 fixture cards is planned. Each card will incorporate taxonomic category chips (e.g., plant, bird, insect), alongside accuracy and refusal rate meters, plus a batch run button.

# Phase 6 — UI Design Contract

> Visual and interaction contract for frontend phases. Generated by gsd-ui-researcher, verified by gsd-ui-checker.

---

## Design System

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Tool | shadcn |
| Preset | Tangerin Dream |
| Component library | base-ui (`@base-ui-components/react`) |
| Icon library | Lucide React (`lucide-react`) |
| Font | Amaranth (sans), Noto Serif (serif), Caveat (handwriting) |

---

## Spacing Scale

Declared values (multiples of 4):

| Token | Value | Usage |
|-------|-------|-------|
| xs | 4px | Icon gaps, inline badge padding |
| sm | 8px | Compact chip padding, input spacing |
| md | 16px | Default card padding, control gaps |
| lg | 24px | Section padding, modal content padding |
| xl | 32px | Dialog layout gaps, page headers |
| 2xl | 48px | Major section breaks, hero spacing |
| 3xl | 64px | Page-level boundary padding |

Exceptions: none

---

## Typography

| Role | Size | Weight | Line Height | Font Family |
|------|------|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Display / Handwriting | 32px–40px | 400 (Regular) | 1.2 | Caveat (`--font-handwriting`, cursive) |
| Heading (H1/H2) | 24px–28px | 700 (Bold) | 1.25 | Noto Serif (`--font-serif`, serif) |
| Label / Pill | 12px–14px | 500 (Medium) | 1.0 | Amaranth (`--font-sans`, sans-serif) |
| Body | 14px–16px | 400 (Regular) | 1.5 | Amaranth (`--font-sans`, sans-serif) |

---

## Color

| Role | Value | Usage |
|------|-------|-------|
| Dominant (60%) | `#FFFDF8` (Light) / `#1C1917` (Dark) | App background, page surfaces |
| Secondary (30%) | `#FBF9F4` (Light) / `#292524` (Dark) | Dialog cards, modal sheets, setting rows |
| Accent (10%) | `#F35C2B` (Terracotta) | Primary CTA buttons, Tegaki pen strokes, active toggles, badge borders |
| Destructive | `#DC2626` | Danger Zone data wipe confirmation |

Accent reserved for: Primary action buttons (`I Understand & Accept`, `Run Batch Evaluation`), active settings toggle thumbs, Tegaki handwriting pen stroke highlights, and verified taxonomic badges.

---

## Copywriting Contract

| Element | Copy |
|---------|------|
| Consent Gate Modal Title | "Welcome to Treads" |
| Consent Gate Primary CTA | "I Understand & Accept" |
| Consent Gate Subtext | "Field journal, species records, high-res photos, and notes remain strictly in your browser's IndexedDB." |
| Permission Denied Banner (Camera) | "Camera access was denied. You can still upload photos from your device files." |
| Permission Denied Banner (Mic) | "Microphone access was denied. You can still type observation notes manually." |
| Permission Denied Banner (GPS) | "Location access was denied. Free-form walking is active without path recording." |
| Storage Persist Granted Badge | "Durable Storage: Protected" |
| Storage Persist Best-Effort Badge | "Durable Storage: Best-effort" |
| Storage Persist Action | "Protect Storage" |
| Tegaki Hero Tagline | "Step outside. Notice what lives." |
| Eval Benchmark Primary CTA | "Run Batch Evaluation" |
| Eval Pass Status Banner | "All evaluation criteria passed: ≥70% Top-3 Accuracy & ≥90% Honest Refusal" |
| Danger Zone Data Reset CTA | "Permanently Erase All Data" |

---

## UI Considerations

Applicable state considerations resolved: 5 covered, 2 backstop, 0 unresolved

| Category | Element(s) | Status | Resolution / Reason |
|----------|------------|--------|---------------------|
| First-time onboarding | `ConsentModal` | ✅ covered | Renders unclosable blocking overlay until user clicks 'I Understand & Accept', then persists acceptance to IndexedDB. |
| Permission denial fallback | Camera/Mic/GPS sheets | ✅ covered | Non-blocking inline banner with guidance and immediate manual fallback (file input for photo, text area for voice). |
| Accessibility / Reduced Motion | `TegakiText` | ✅ covered | If `prefers-reduced-motion` is active, handwriting animation duration is 0ms, rendering instant static text. |
| Autoplay policy | `Cuelume` Web Audio | ✅ covered | AudioContext initialized/resumed only on explicit user click/tap, avoiding browser console autoplay warnings. |
| Muted state | Settings toggles | ✅ covered | Sound chimes default to OFF; haptics default to ON; respects user toggles in `db.settings`. |
| Network latency | `/eval` batch runner | 🧪 backstop | Progress bar with animated percentage pulse and disabled button state during evaluation execution. |
| Mobile viewport responsiveness | Modal & HUD sheets | 🧪 backstop | `max-h-[90vh]` with overflow-y-auto and touch padding prevents clipping on Android mobile viewports. |

---

## Registry Safety

| Registry | Blocks Used | Safety Gate |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| shadcn official | dialog, badge, button, progress, card | not required |
| base-ui primitives | dialog, popover, sheet | verified compatible with React 19 |

---

- [x] Dimension 2 Visuals: PASS
- [x] Dimension 3 Color: PASS
- [x] Dimension 4 Typography: PASS
- [x] Dimension 5 Spacing: PASS
- [x] Dimension 6 Registry Safety: PASS

# Plan 06-01: Tegaki Handwriting Animation, Cuelume Web Audio Chimes, Haptics & Consent Gate

## Objective
Implement sensory polish and privacy enforcement: build the progressive Tegaki handwriting reveal component with Google Font Caveat fallback (`DSGN-03`), synthesize gentle dual-oscillator Cuelume Web Audio chimes for capture and hunt win (`DSGN-04`), trigger native device haptic vibrations (`DSGN-05`), and enforce the global first-run consent modal gate with `navigator.storage.persist()` and non-blocking permission fallbacks (`CONS-01`, `CONS-02`, `CONS-03`, `CONS-04`).

## User Rules & Context
- **SHELL:** zsh
- **Package Manager:** pnpm
- **Design Contract:** Follow Tangerin Dream tokens, 4-multiple spacing scale, typography hierarchy, and Caveat font token in `06-UI-SPEC.md`.
- **Locked Decisions (per CONTEXT.md):**
  - **D-01:** SVG path stroke dashoffset / cursive draw over ~1.2s.
  - **D-02:** Google Font Caveat cursive fallback with instant opacity reveal when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active.
  - **D-03:** Scope: Landing hero headline and Fact Card confirmed specimen titles; plays once on view entrance.
  - **D-04:** Dynamic text rendering: SVG text stroke with dashoffset reveal + Caveat cursive styling scaling to arbitrary species names.
  - **D-05:** Dual-sine / triangle warm chime with exponential decay envelope (gentle brass/field bell feel).
  - **D-06:** 2 events: Specimen Confirmation (E5-G#5) & Daily Hunt Completion (C5-E5-G5-C6).
  - **D-07:** Tactile pair: crisp 25ms tick on capture/selection, and resonant double pulse [40ms, 60ms, 80ms] on confirmation/hunt win.
  - **D-08:** Audio chimes OFF by default, Haptics ON by default; lazy `AudioContext` resume on first user interaction.
  - **D-09:** Strict app-wide modal overlay on first visit blocking interaction until accepted.
  - **D-10:** Semver string `"1.0.0"` & timestamp in `db.settings`.
  - **D-11:** Non-blocking inline banner with guidance and immediate manual fallback (file picker, text note) on permission denial.
  - **D-12:** Silent request on consent click; live status badge in `/settings` with one-tap retry button.

Before dispatching on a built-in-only runtime (kimi-code — three built-ins only), resolve the role to a built-in via `gsd_run query resolve-dispatch-type --requested <role> --raw`. 20: <runtime_compatibility>
21: **Subagent spawning is runtime-specific:**
22: - **Claude Code:** Uses `Agent(subagent_type="gsd-executor", ...)` — backgrounded by default; verify completion
23: - **Copilot:** Subagent spawning does not reliably return completion signals. **Default to
24:   sequential inline execution**: read and follow execute-plan.md directly for each plan
25:   instead of spawning parallel agents. Only attempt parallel spawning if the user
26:   explicitly requests it — and in that case, rely on the spot-check fallback in step 3
27:   to detect completion.
28: - **Other runtimes:** If `Agent`/`agent` tool is genuinely unavailable (e.g. a backgrounded
29:   Claude Code agent per #853, or a non-the agent runtime), use sequential inline execution as
30:   the fallback for executor parallelization only. If `Agent` IS available (top-level the agent
31:   Code), you MUST spawn gsd-executor agents — inline execution is not authorized. Check for
32:   actual tool availability, not runtime name.
33: 
34: **Fallback rule:** If a spawned agent completes its work (commits visible, SUMMARY.md exists) but
35: the orchestrator never receives the completion signal, treat it as successful based on spot-checks
36: and continue to the next wave/plan. Never block indefinitely waiting for a signal — always verify
37: via filesystem and git state.

120: if [ -f .gitmodules ]; then

The auto-degrade prints a one-line warning to stderr and falls through to the sequential path so executors do not hit the exit-42 worktree-branch-check halt. args.CodeContent:
# Treads Outdoor Field Verification Protocol

This document defines the standardized manual verification protocol for real-world testing of **Treads** (`treads.local` or deployed instance) on a mobile device outdoors.

---

## Prerequisites
- Mobile browser (iOS Safari, Android Chrome, or mobile Chromium).
- Location services enabled on device.
- Camera and microphone permissions allowed.
- Outdoor or garden environment with natural organisms (plants, trees, insects, birds).

---

## Verification Protocol Steps

### 1. First-Run Consent Gate & Persistent Storage (`CONS-01`, `CONS-02`, `CONS-03`)
1. Open the application in an incognito or fresh browser session.
2. **Observe**: The app-wide blocking modal overlay (`Welcome to Treads`) appears immediately.
3. Verify that tapping the background or pressing back/escape does not dismiss the modal (`disablePointerDismissal`).
4. Read the 4 privacy pillars:
   - AI Vision Identification (ephemeral Gemini analysis)
   - Voice Transcription (ephemeral ElevenLabs transcription)
   - Pedestrian Routing (coarse routing via OpenRouteService)
   - 100% On-Device Journal (local IndexedDB persistence)
5. Tap **"I Understand & Accept"**.
6. **Verify**: Modal dismisses, consent version `1.0.0` and timestamp are written to `db.settings`, and `navigator.storage.persist()` is silently invoked.
7. Navigate to `/settings` and verify the persistence status badge reads `Persisted` (or `Best Effort` with a manual retry button).

### 2. Live Walk Session & Geolocation Tracking (`WALK-01`, `WALK-02`, `WALK-03`)
1. From home, navigate to `/walk`.
2. Tap **"Start Free Walk"** (or generate a suggested loop).
3. **Observe**: Map centers on the live GPS coordinate pin.
4. Walk at least 50 meters outdoors.
5. **Verify**:
   - GPS accuracy filter suppresses erratic readings (>35m accuracy rejected).
   - Breadcrumb polyline trail renders smoothly behind your current position.
   - Live walk metrics update: elapsed duration timer and distance traveled in meters.

### 3. Two-Tap Specimen Capture, Sensory Cuelume Chime & Haptics (`CAPT-01`, `DSGN-04`, `DSGN-05`)
1. Stop at an observed plant, tree, or insect.
2. Tap the large circular **Camera** button in the walk dock.
3. Snap a clear photo of the specimen.
4. **Observe**: EXIF GPS metadata is scrubbed client-side before sending to Gemini.
5. In the candidate drawer, review up to 3 taxonomic candidates with confidence ratings (`Likely`, `Possible`, `Unsure`).
6. Tap the checkmark on the matching candidate.
7. **Verify**:
   - Dual-oscillator Cuelume chime plays (warm major-third dual tone E5 659.25Hz -> G#5 830.61Hz with exponential decay).
   - Device triggers a crisp tactile vibration (`[25ms]` on tap, `[40ms, 60ms, 80ms]` on confirmation).
   - Candidate is recorded into the local IndexedDB journal.

### 4. Progressive Tegaki Handwriting & Wikipedia Fact Cards (`DSGN-03`, `SPEC-01`)
1. Tap the specimen card or open `/entry/[id]`.
2. **Observe**: The confirmed common name renders via **Tegaki handwriting reveal** (`Caveat` cursive stroke wipe across ~1.2s).
3. Review the Wikipedia educational facts. Tap any of the 3 bullet points to expand sentence-level verified Wikipedia citations.

1. On the walk screen or entry detail, tap the **Microphone** icon.
2. Speak a field note (e.g., "Noticed early morning dew on petals, solitary bee foraging nearby").
3. **Observe**: Live canvas waveform visualizes microphone input.
4. Tap Stop: speech note is saved to IndexedDB and transcribed.
5. Tap **"Listen to Field Summary"**: ElevenLabs natural voice reads the summary with cached audio replay.

### 7. Life List & Journal Review (`JOUR-01`, `JOUR-02`)
1. Tap End Walk -> Save Walk.

args.CodeContent:
# Treads 🌿

> *Step outside. Notice what lives.*

Treads is a mindful, local-first naturalist companion that turns outdoor walks into observational field journals. It combines pedestrian loop generation, on-device AI species identification, Wikipedia-verified naturalist notes, voice observation capture, tactile sensory cues, and one-tap Obsidian vault exports.

Built for the **Google AI Studio / Gemini Naturalist Challenge**.

---

## Key Highlights

- **🔒 100% Local-First & Privacy Sovereign (`CONS-01` - `CONS-04`):**
  - All field observations, GPS breadcrumbs, photos, and voice notes live directly in browser IndexedDB.
  - EXIF GPS metadata is stripped before client queries.
  - Strict first-visit privacy consent gate with durable storage request (`navigator.storage.persist()`).

- **🧭 Pedestrian Loop Navigation (`WALK-01` - `WALK-03`):**
  - Interactive MapLibre GL vector maps with outdoor topography tiles.
  - Suggested walking loops (15m, 30m, 45m) generated via OpenRouteService pedestrian routing.
  - Background-resilient GPS tracking with 35m accuracy filtering and automatic wake resumption.

- **🔍 Two-Tap Taxonomic Species Identification (`CAPT-01`, `EVAL-01`):**
  - Multimodal vision identification powered by Google Gemini.
  - Returns up to 3 candidate species with taxonomic ranks and confidence scoring.
  - Honest refusal engine refusing non-living inanimate objects and human portraits.
  - Headless 30-fixture evaluation suite (`pnpm test:eval`) verifying ≥70% organism accuracy and ≥90% honest refusal rate.

- **📖 Wikipedia Educational Fact Cards (`SPEC-01`):**
  - Three verified sentence-level natural history facts linked to source Wikipedia citations.
  - Cached for offline retrieval.

- **🖋️ Tegaki Handwriting & Cuelume Sensory Polish (`DSGN-03` - `DSGN-05`):**
  - Progressive Japanese Tegaki-style ink handwriting reveal with `Caveat` font and `prefers-reduced-motion` bypass.
  - Dual-oscillator synthesized Web Audio chimes (E5–G#5 major third capture chime, C5–E5–G5–C6 celebration arpeggio).
  - Tactile native haptic vibration (`navigator.vibrate`) on capture and hunt victory.

- **🎙️ Voice Observation Notes & Speech (`VOIC-01`, `VOIC-02`):**
  - Voice recording with live canvas waveform visualization.
  - ElevenLabs speech-to-text transcription and high-fidelity text-to-speech naturalist narration.

- **🎯 Daily Species Hunt Challenge (`HUNT-01`, `HUNT-02`):**
  - Daily rotation of naturalist targets (birds, trees, insects, fungi).
  - Celebration dialog and celebratory audio/haptic rewards on fulfillment.

- **📓 Obsidian-Compatible Vault Export (`EXP-01`, `EXP-02`):**
  - One-tap export generating a zip archive containing Markdown notes with YAML frontmatter, organized photos, and full database backup.

---

## Tech Stack

- **Framework:** Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack) & React 19
- **UI & Tokens:** Tailwind CSS v4, Base UI primitives, Lucide React, Tangerin Dream design tokens
- **Database:** Dexie 4.4 (IndexedDB) with `dexie-react-hooks`
- **Maps:** MapLibre GL 6.13
- **AI & Speech:** Google Gemini (`@ai-sdk/google`, `ai`), ElevenLabs API
- **Audio & Motion:** Web Audio API (Cuelume dual-oscillator synthesizer), Motion

---

## Getting Started

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
pnpm install
```

### 2. Environment Variables
Create a `.env.local` file with the following keys:
```bash
# Google AI Studio (Gemini)
GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key

# ElevenLabs (Voice transcription & TTS)
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your_elevenlabs_api_key

# OpenRouteService (Pedestrian loops)
OPENROUTESERVICE_API_KEY=your_ors_api_key
```

### 3. Run Development Server
```bash
pnpm dev
```
Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser.

### 4. Headless Evaluation Benchmark
Run the automated 30-fixture taxonomic identification and refusal test suite:
```bash
pnpm test:eval
```

### 5. Production Build
```bash
pnpm build
```

---

## Field Verification

See [`FIELD-VERIFICATION.md`](./FIELD-VERIFICATION.md) for the 8-step outdoor field walkthrough protocol.

---

## License
MIT

426: <step name="reconcile_gaps">
427: **Reconcile diagnosed gaps against completed gap-closure plans (#1921):**

429: When verify-work resumes after `/gsd-execute-phase --gaps-only`, the UAT `## Gaps` entries still read `status: failed` even though their fix plans have executed. Without reconciliation verify-work re-diagnoses them as fresh blockers and spawns new gap plans — losing the verification state. This step closes the loop.

433: 2. If such a plan exists AND has a matching `*-SUMMARY.md` in the phase dir (the plan was executed by `--gaps-only`), the gap is **resolved** — update its YAML in place:
434:    ```yaml
435:    - gap_id: G-{phase}-{N}
436:      status: resolved        # was: failed
437:      resolved_by: {plan basename}
438:      resolved_at: {today}
439:    ```
440: 3. If no plan references the `gap_id`, or the plan has no SUMMARY, leave the gap `status: failed` (still open).
441: 
442: Read plan frontmatter directly in-context — do not pipe it through a shell parser. After reconciliation, announce:
443: ```
444: Reconciled gap-closure state: {resolved_count} gap(s) resolved by executed plans, {open_count} still open.
445: ```
446: 
447: Resolved gaps are NOT re-diagnosed and do NOT spawn new gap plans. If the user later reports the same behavior as still broken, treat it as a new issue (a regression) with a fresh `gap_id`.
448: </step>
